paragraphs: Bloomin' Brands, Inc. ("Bloomin' Brands," the "Company," "we," "us," and "our" and similar terms mean Bloomin' Brands, Inc. and its subsidiaries except where the context otherwise requires), a Delaware corporation, is one of the largest casual dining restaurant companies in the world, with a portfolio of leading, differentiated restaurant concepts. Our restaurant portfolio includes Outback Steakhouse, Carrabba's Italian Grill, Bonefish Grill and Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar. Our restaurant concepts range in price point and degree of formality from casual (Outback Steakhouse and Carrabba's Italian Grill) to polished casual (Bonefish Grill) and fine dining (Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar). OSI Restaurant Partners, LLC ("OSI"), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Bloomin' Brands, is our primary operating entity.

As of December 28, 2025, we owned and operated 967 restaurants and franchised 493 restaurants across 46 states, Guam and 12 countries. On December 30, 2024, we completed the sale of the majority ownership of our Brazil operations, and all restaurants in that market are now operated as unconsolidated franchisees. See International Franchise Segment discussion below for details.

We consider each of our U.S. restaurant concepts and international franchise markets to be operating segments, which reflects how we manage our business, review operating performance and allocate resources. We aggregate our U.S. operating segments into the U.S. reportable segment. The U.S. segment includes all restaurants operating in the U.S. while franchised restaurants operating outside the U.S. are included in the international franchise segment. All other operating segments, which include the Company's operations in Hong Kong and the equity method investment in Brazil, do not meet the quantitative thresholds for determining reportable operating segments. Following is a summary of reportable segments as of December 28, 2025:

Carrabba's Italian Grill Bonefish Grill Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar International Franchise (2)

As of December 28, 2025, in our U.S. segment, we owned and operated 957 restaurants and franchised 138 restaurants across 46 states.

Outback Steakhouse - Outback Steakhouse is a casual steakhouse restaurant concept focused on steaks, bold flavors and Australian decor. The Outback Steakhouse menu offers seasoned and seared grilled steaks, ribs, chicken, seafood, pasta, salads and seasonal specials. The menu also offers a selection of specialty appetizers, including our signature Bloomin' Onion®, and desserts, together with full bar service.

Carrabba's Italian Grill - Offering authentic Italian cuisine passed down from its founders' family recipes, Carrabba's Italian Grill uses high-quality ingredients to prepare fresh and handmade dishes cooked to order in a lively exhibition kitchen. Featuring a wood-burning grill inspired by the many tastes of Italy, guests can enjoy
signature dishes such as Chicken Bryan and Pollo Rosa Maria, wood-fire grilled steaks and chops, and classic Italian pasta dishes in a welcoming, contemporary atmosphere.

Bonefish Grill - Bonefish Grill specializes in fish from around the world, hand-cut in-house every day, savory wood-grilled specialties and locally created, seasonal Partner Selection dishes featuring high-quality and fresh ingredients. Offering a selection of classic and signature hand-crafted cocktails, using fresh juices, edible garnishes and house infusions, Bonefish Grill also features a distinct list of wines, the perfect match for any food pairing.

Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar - Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar is a contemporary interpretation of the classic American steakhouse, boasting culinary mastery, signature style and unrivaled attentive service to create memorable dining experiences for guests. Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar offers an impressive range of USDA Prime steaks, premium seafood entrées, storied wines and fresh hand-crafted cocktails.

On December 30, 2024, we sold 67% of our Brazil operations (the "Brazil Sale Transaction") and retained a 33% interest. Following the sale, restaurants that were formerly Company-owned now operate as unconsolidated franchisees.

headings: Risks Related to the Restaurant Industry
Food safety and food-borne illness concerns in our restaurants or throughout the industry or supply chain may have an adverse effect on our business by reducing demand and increasing costs.
Failure to recruit, train and retain high-quality leadership, restaurant-level management and hourly team members may inhibit our ability to operate and grow successfully.

The food service industry is affected by consumer preferences and perceptions. Changes in these preferences and perceptions may lessen the demand for our products, which would reduce sales and harm our business.
Our inability or failure to recognize, respond to and effectively manage the accelerated impact of social media could have a material adverse impact on our business.
Risks Related to Government Regulation
We are subject to various federal and state employment and labor laws and regulations.
Our failure to comply with government regulation related to our restaurant operations, and the costs of compliance or non-compliance, could adversely affect our business.
Changes in tax laws, uncertainty in the judicial interpretation of those laws and unanticipated tax liabilities could adversely affect the taxes we pay and our profitability.

If we fail to adequately address corporate citizenship and sustainability matters, it could have an adverse effect on our business, financial condition, and operating results and may damage our reputation.
Risks Related to Our Business Model and Strategy

Failure to execute successfully our turnaround strategy or to achieve projected cost savings from our efficiency initiatives could adversely affect our results of operations and limit growth opportunities for our brands.

Our success depends substantially on the value of our brands and our ability to execute innovative marketing and consumer relationship initiatives to maintain brand relevance and drive profitable sales growth.
There are risks and uncertainties associated with strategic actions and initiatives that we may implement.
We have limited control with respect to the operations of our franchisees and the business challenges they face, which could have a negative impact on our business.
Risks associated with our remodeling, relocation and expansion plans may have adverse effects on our operating results.
We face a variety of risks associated with doing business in foreign markets that could have a negative impact on our financial performance.
Risks Related to Inflation and Macroeconomic Disruption
Challenging economic, political and social conditions may have a negative effect on our business and financial results.
Increased commodity, energy and other costs could decrease our profit margins or cause us to limit or otherwise modify our menus or increase prices, which could adversely affect our business.
Risks Related to Information Technology, Privacy and Intellectual Property
Our failure or inability to enforce our trademarks or other proprietary rights could adversely affect our competitive position or the value of our brand.
Risks Related to Our Indebtedness
Our leverage could adversely affect our ability to raise additional capital to fund our operations or limit our ability to react to changes in the economy or our industry.
Our debt agreements contain restrictions that limit our flexibility in operating our business.
Risks Related to Our Common Stock
Our stock price is subject to volatility.
paragraphs: The risk factors set forth below should be carefully considered. The risks described below are those that we believe could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations, however, they are not the only risks facing us. Additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us or those we currently view to be immaterial may also materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations.

Regardless of the source or cause, any report of food-borne illnesses and other food safety issues, whether at one of our restaurants, in the industry or supply chain, could have a negative impact on our traffic and sales and adversely affect the reputation of our brands. Food safety issues could be caused by suppliers or distributors and, as a result, be out of our control and this risk may be exacerbated by supply chain issues, which could delay deliveries and necessitate alternative sourcing on short notice. Health concerns or outbreaks of disease in a food product could also reduce demand for particular menu offerings. Even instances of food-borne illness, food tampering or contamination occurring solely at other company's restaurants could result in negative publicity about the food service industry and adversely impact our sales. There is also the risk of allergen cross contamination in our restaurants despite precautionary measures to minimize the risk. Social media has dramatically increased the rate at which negative publicity, including as it relates to food-borne illnesses, can be disseminated before there is any meaningful opportunity to respond or address an issue. The occurrence of food-borne illnesses or food safety issues could also adversely affect the price and availability of affected ingredients, resulting in higher costs and lower margins.

The restaurant industry is highly competitive and consumer options for other prepared food offerings continue to expand. Our inability to compete effectively could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.

A substantial number of restaurant operators compete directly and indirectly with us with respect to price, service, location and food quality, some of which are well-established with significant resources. There is also active competition for management, team members and other personnel, and attractive suitable real estate sites. Consumer tastes, nutritional and dietary trends, traffic patterns, discretionary spending habits and the type, number and location of competing restaurants often affect the restaurant business, and our competitors may react more efficiently, creatively and effectively to those conditions. In addition, our competitors may generate or better implement business strategies that improve the value and relevance of their brands and reputation, relative to ours. For example, our competitors may more successfully implement menu or technology initiatives, such as remote ordering, social media or mobile technology platforms that expedite or enhance the customer experience, or artificial intelligence to develop new customer insights. Further, we face growing competition from quick service and fast-casual restaurants, the supermarket industry and meal kit and food delivery providers, with the improvement of prepared food offerings. and the trend towards convergence in grocery, deli, delivery, retail and restaurant services. Further, if this competitive environment and the breadth of alternatives result in a decline in casual dining customer traffic, it could make our financial operations dependent on our ability to increase our market share within the hyper-competitive casual dining segment. We believe all of the above factors have increased competitive pressures in the casual dining sector in recent periods and we believe they will continue to present a challenging competitive environment in future periods. If we are unable to continue to compete effectively, our traffic, sales and margins could decline and our business, financial condition and results of operations would be adversely affected.

Our success will continue to depend, to a significant extent, on our leadership team and other key management personnel. For example, during 2025, we appointed a new chief financial officer and made other changes to our senior leadership team. While some of these changes were reflective of ongoing succession-planning, leadership transition can create risks as individuals are integrated into new roles, onboarding shifts management attention from business concerns, we may fail to retain other key personnel, or we may lose institutional knowledge. These risks and uncertainties could result in operational and administrative inefficiencies and additional added costs, which could adversely impact our results of operations.

Our restaurant-level management and team members are largely responsible for the quality of our service. Our guests may be dissatisfied and our sales may decline if we fail to recruit, train and retain managers and team members that effectively implement our business strategy and provide high-quality guest service. There is active competition for quality management personnel and hourly team members, and such competition could require us to pay higher wages or incur higher costs for retaining and incentivizing our management personnel and hourly team members. If we experience high turnover, we may experience higher labor costs and have a shortage of adequate management personnel required for future growth. The tight labor market in the United States has further strained and could continue to strain our ability to keep our restaurants fully staffed. A shortage of team members also could cause our restaurants to operate with reduced staff, which could adversely affect our ability to provide high-quality guest service and cause our business and financial results to suffer.

paragraphs: Management's discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and the related notes. We have classified the results of operations, non-GAAP measures, and liquidity and capital resources of our Brazil operations as discontinued operations for all periods presented. Unless otherwise noted, this Management Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations does not include discontinued operations.

We utilize a 52-53-week year ending on the last Sunday in December. In a 52-week fiscal year, each quarterly period is comprised of 13 weeks. The additional week in a 53-week fiscal year is added to the fourth quarter. Fiscal years 2025 and 2024 both consisted of 52 weeks. For discussion of our consolidated and segment-level results of operations, non-GAAP measures, and liquidity and capital resources not included in this Annual Report for fiscal year 2023, see our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 29, 2024, filed with the SEC on February 26, 2025.

We are one of the largest casual dining restaurant companies in the world with a portfolio of leading, differentiated restaurant concepts. As of December 28, 2025, we owned and operated 967 restaurants and franchised 493 restaurants across 46 states, Guam and 12 countries. Our restaurant portfolio includes: Outback Steakhouse, Carrabba's Italian Grill, Bonefish Grill and Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar.
Financial Overview - Our financial overview for 2025 includes the following:
•U.S. combined and Outback Steakhouse comparable restaurant sales of 0.2% and (0.5)%, respectively;
•Increase in Total revenues of 0.1% as compared to 2024;
•Operating income and restaurant-level operating margins of 0.9% and 11.7%, respectively, as compared to 3.5% and 13.3%, respectively for 2024;
•Operating income of $37.2 million as compared to $139.8 million in 2024; and
•Diluted earnings per share of $0.10 as compared to diluted loss per share of $(0.61) in 2024.

Sale of Majority Ownership of our Brazil Operations - On December 30, 2024, we completed the sale of 67% of our Brazil operations (the "Brazil Sale Transaction") and entered into amended and restated franchise agreements with all existing restaurants in Brazil. The balance sheets, results of operations and cash flows of our Brazil operations are reported as discontinued operations for all periods presented. See Note 2 - Discontinued Operations of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for additional details.

Our Turnaround Strategy - In November 2025, we announced a comprehensive turnaround strategy, with a key focus on Outback Steakhouse, to drive long-term sustainable and profitable growth. This strategy is based on four key platforms, including:

•Deliver a Remarkable Dine-In Experience: focus on operational excellence with center of the plate quality and service enhancements to deliver exceptional guest experience, which will drive in-restaurant traffic growth.
•Drive Brand Relevancy: expand brand reach to recruit new guests and increase frequency of visits.
•Reignite a Culture of Ownership and Fun: reinvest in our people and strengthen our Principles & Beliefs-based culture which will drive an enhanced guest experience.

Outback Steakhouse - Outback Steakhouse 是一家休閒風格的牛排餐廳概念，專注於牛排、濃鬱風味與澳洲裝潢。Outback Steakhouse 餐單提供調味過的牛排、肋排、雞肉、海鮮、義大利麵、沙拉與季節限定餐點。餐單也提供多樣化的前菜選擇，包括我們的招牌 Bloomin' Onion®，以及甜點，並搭配完整的酒吧服務。
Carrabba's Italian Grill - 提供源自創始家族食譜的正宗義大利料理，Carrabba's Italian Grill 使用高品質食材，製作新鮮且手工製作的餐點，並在活潑的展示廚房中現點現做。特色為木炭烤爐，靈感來自義大利多樣的風味，顧客可享用
招牌餐點如 Chicken Bryan 和 Pollo Rosa Maria、木炭烤牛排與牛柳，以及經典義大利麵料理，於溫馨現代的氛圍中享用。
Bonefish Grill - Bonefish Grill 專注於來自世界各地的魚類，每日現場切割，並提供風味濃鬱的木炭烤料理與當地創意、季節限定的 Partner Selection 餐點，使用高品質與新鮮食材。提供多樣化的經典與招牌手作雞尾酒，使用新鮮果汁、可食用裝飾與自製調味料，Bonefish Grill 也提供獨特的葡萄酒選項，完美搭配任何餐點。

Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar - Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar 是對經典美國牛排餐廳的現代詮釋，擁有精湛的廚藝、獨特風格與無與倫比的貼心服務，為顧客創造難忘的用餐體驗。Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar 提供廣泛的 USDA Prime 牛排、高級海鮮主菜、知名葡萄酒與新鮮手作雞尾酒。

paragraphs: 管理階層對於財務狀況與營運成果之討論分析，應與我們之合併財務報表及其相關附註一併閱讀。我們已將巴西營運之營運成果、非GAAP指標及流動性與資本資源歸類為已終止營運，適用於所有呈報期間。除非另有說明，本管理討論與分析財務狀況與營運成果之內容不包含已終止營運之項目。
我們採用52至53週財務年度，於12月最後一個星期日結算。在52週財務年度中，每季為13週。在53週財務年度中，多出的一週會加入第四季。2025財務年度與2024財務年度皆為52週。有關我們合併財務與分部層面營運成果、非GAAP指標及流動性與資本資源之討論，如未包含於本年度報告中，請參閱我們2024年12月29日結算之年度報告（Form 10-K），該報告已於2025年2月26日提交至SEC。

我們是全球最大的休閒餐飲連鎖餐廳公司之一，擁有領先且差異化的餐廳品牌組合。截至2025年12月28日，我們擁有並營運967間餐廳，並特許經營493間餐廳，分佈於46個州、關島及12個國家。我們的餐廳組合包括：Outback Steakhouse、Carrabba's Italian Grill、Bonefish Grill及Fleming's Prime Steakhouse & Wine Bar。
財務概觀 - 我們2025年之財務概觀包含以下內容：
•美國合併營運與Outback Steakhouse同店比較營業額成長為0.2%及(0.5)%；
•總營收較2024年成長0.1%；
•營運獲利與餐廳層級營運毛利率分別為0.9%及11.7%，較2024年之3.5%及13.3%；
•營運收入為 37.2 百萬美元，較 2024 年的 139.8 百萬美元
•每股稀釋收益為 0.10 美元，較 2024 年每股稀釋虧損為 (0.61) 美元。
出售我們巴西營運的多數股權 - 於 2024 年 12 月 30 日，我們完成出售我們巴西營運 67% 的股權（"巴西出售交易"），並與巴西所有現有餐廳簽訂修正後的特許經營協議。我們巴西營運的資產負債表、營運成果及現金流，於所有呈列期間均列為已終止營運。有關更多細節，請參閱財務報表附註第 2 項 - 已終止營運。
我們的扭轉策略 - 於 2025 年 11 月，我們宣佈一項全面扭轉策略，重點聚焦 Outback Steakhouse，以推動長期可持續且有利潤的成長。此策略基於四大關鍵平台，包括：
•提供卓越的用餐體驗：專注於運營卓越，提升餐點品質與服務，以提供卓越的顧客體驗，進而推動餐廳內人流量成長。
•提升品牌相關性：擴大品牌影響力，招募新顧客並提高造訪頻率。
•重燃擁有感與樂趣的文化：重新投資於我們的員工，強化以原則與信念為基礎的文化，以提供更優質的顧客體驗。

headings: 與餐飲業相關的風險
本公司餐廳或整個產業或供應鏈所面臨的食品安全及食源性疾病問題，可能對本公司業務產生負面影響，導致需求減少且成本增加。
未能招募、培訓及留住高素質的領導層、餐廳層管理階層及時薪員工，可能限制本公司成功運營及成長的能力。
餐飲業受消費者偏好及觀感影響，這些偏好及觀感的變化可能降低對本公司產品的需求，進而減少銷售額並損害本公司業務。
本公司未能識別、回應及有效管理社交媒體加速影響的風險，可能對本公司業務產生重大負面影響。
與政府規範相關的風險
本公司受美國聯邦及州政府就僱用及勞動事項所訂定的法律及規範所規範。
本公司未能遵守與餐廳營運相關的政府規範，以及因遵守或未遵守規範而產生的成本，可能對本公司業務產生負面影響。
稅法的變更、司法對這些法律的解釋不確定性以及未預見的稅務負擔，可能會不利於我們所支付的稅款及營業利潤。
若我們未能妥善處理企業公民責任及可持續性相關事項，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運結果產生不利影響，並可能損害我們的聲譽。
與我們商業模式及策略相關的風險
若我們未能成功執行扭轉策略，或未能達成效率提升計畫預期的節省成本，可能會對我們的營運結果產生不利影響，並限制我們品牌成長的機會。
我們的成敗在很大程度上取決於我們品牌的價值，以及我們執行創新行銷及消費者關係計畫的能力，以維持品牌相關性並推動獲利性銷售成長。
我們可能實施的戰略行動及計畫，存在風險與不確定性。
我們對特許經營商的營運及他們所面臨的業務挑戰控制有限，這可能會對我們的業務產生負面影響。
與我們翻新、遷移及擴張計畫相關的風險，可能會對我們的營運結果產生不利影響。
我們面臨許多與在海外市場營運相關的風險，這些風險可能對我們的財務表現產生負面影響。
與通貨膨脹及總體經濟幹擾相關的風險
艱難的經濟、政治及社會環境可能對我們的業務及財務結果產生負面影響。
增加的原物料、能源及其他成本可能降低我們的毛利率，或導致我們限制或以其他方式調整產品項目或提高價格，這可能會對我們的業務產生負面影響。
與資訊科技、隱私權及智慧財產權相關的風險
我們未能執行或無法強制執行我們的商標或其他專有權利，可能會對我們的競爭地位或品牌的價值產生負面影響。
與我們的負債相關的風險
我們的負債程度可能影響我們籌措額外資金以支應營運的能力，或限制我們對經濟或產業變動的反應能力。

paragraphs: 風險因素如下所述，請謹慎考量。下列所述的風險是我們認為可能對我們的業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大且不利影響的風險，然而，這些並非我們所面臨的唯一風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉，或目前認為不重要，也可能對我們的業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大且不利影響。

無論來源或原因為何，任何有關食源性疾病或其他食品安全問題的報導，無論發生在本公司餐廳、產業或供應鏈中，都可能對我們的客流量與銷售造成負面影響，並損害我們品牌的聲譽。食品安全問題可能由供應商或分銷商造成，因此可能超出我們的控制範圍，此風險可能因供應鏈問題而更加嚴重，可能導致交貨延誤，並需要短時間內尋找替代來源。食品產品的健康問題或疾病爆發也可能降低特定餐點的 demand。即使食源性疾病、食品篡改或污染僅發生在其他公司的餐廳中，也可能導致有關餐飲產業的負面宣傳，並對我們的銷售造成不利影響。此外，儘管我們已採取預防措施以降低風險，但我們的餐廳仍可能發生過敏原交叉污染的風險。社交媒體大幅增加了負面宣傳，包括與食源性疾病相關的宣傳，傳播的速度，使得在有足夠時間回應或處理問題之前，就已廣為散佈。
餐飲產業競爭激烈，消費者對其他即食食品的選擇持續擴張。我們若無法有效競爭，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成不利影響。

大量餐飲業者與我們在價格、服務、地點及食品品質方面直接或間接競爭，其中一些業者已建立良好聲譽且擁有大量資源。此外，對於管理階層、團隊成員及其他員工的競爭也非常活躍，且吸引人的合適零售地點也存在競爭。消費者口味、營養與飲食趨勢、客流量、自由支配開支習慣，以及競爭餐廳的種類、數量與位置，往往影響餐飲業的營運，而我們的競爭對手可能更有效、更具創意與更有效地應對這些情況。此外，我們的競爭對手可能產生或更有效地實施商業策略，以提升其品牌與聲譽的價值與相關性，相較於我們。例如，他們可能更成功地實施餐點或科技方案，如遠端點餐、社交媒體或行動科技平台，以加快或提升顧客體驗，或利用人工智慧來開發新的顧客洞察。此外，我們面臨來自速食與快速餐飲餐廳、超市產業及餐點組合與食品配送供應商的日益增長的競爭，隨著即食食品選擇的改善，以及零售、餐飲、配送與超市服務趨向整合的趨勢。此外，若此競爭環境及選擇的廣度導致休閒餐飲客流量下降，可能會使我們的財務運作依賴於我們在高度競爭的休閒餐飲市場中增加市佔率的能力。我們認為上述因素在近期已增加休閒餐飲產業的競爭壓力，我們相信這些因素在未來期間仍將持續形成具有挑戰性的競爭環境。若我們無法持續有效競爭，我們的客流量、銷售與毛利率可能會下降，並對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成不利影響。

我們的業務能否持續成功，在很大程度上依賴於我們的領導團隊及其他關鍵管理人員。例如，在 2025 年，我們聘任了一位新的首席財務官並對高階領導團隊進行了其他調整。雖然部分調整反映了持續的繼任計畫，但領導層轉換可能帶來風險，因個體適應新角色時，可能分散管理層對業務問題的關注，我們可能無法留住其他關鍵人員，或可能失去機構知識。這些風險與不確定性可能導致營運與行政效率低下及額外成本增加，這可能會對我們的營運成果造成不利影響。

我們的餐廳層級管理與團隊成員主要負責我們服務的品質。若我們未能招募、培訓並留住能有效落實我們商業策略並提供高品質顧客服務的管理與團隊成員，我們的顧客可能會不滿意，導致銷售下降。對於優質管理人員與時薪團隊成員的競爭非常活躍，這種競爭可能導致我們必須支付更高的工資或承擔更高的成本以留住並激勵我們的管理人員與時薪團隊成員。若我們經歷高離職率，可能會導致更高的勞動成本，並缺乏未來成長所需的足夠管理人員。美國緊繃的勞動市場已進一步影響我們維持餐廳滿編的能力，並可能持續影響。團隊成員的短缺也可能導致我們的餐廳以減少人手運作，這可能會影響我們提供高品質顧客服務的能力，並導致我們的業務與財務結果受損。
